question.problem:
Select the missing parts in a particular solution of the differential equation ${y}^{″}-16y=f(x),$ where the Fourier series of the $4$-periodic forcing function is given by

$$
f(x)∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

*Hint: You may assume that the free term and all the sine coefficients in the Fourier series of the particular solution are equal to zero.*

The Fourier series of a particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,{{field-1}}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})
$$
question.worked_solution:
We assume that a solution of our equation has the following Fourier series:

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, we compute the derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{p}^{′} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{n\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}) \\ {y}_{p}^{″} & ∼\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{n\pi }{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the expressions for ${y}_{p}^{″}$ and ${y}_{p}$ into the equation and have

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})-16({\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}))={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get 

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }-{a}_{n}(\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}+16)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2})={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{4}{{n}^{2}}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$

Now, equating the cosine coefficients, we obtain 

$$
-{a}_{n}(\frac{{n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}}{4}+16)=\frac{4}{{n}^{2}}\,⇒\,{a}_{n}=-\frac{16}{{n}^{2}({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+64)}.
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
{y}_{p}∼{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\,-\frac{16}{{n}^{2}({n}^{2}{\pi }^{2}+64)}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi x}{2}).
$$
